To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) exposure reciprocity exists in the polymerization of resin composite, and (2) the degree of reciprocity varies with the composition of the resin composite.

(i) the polymerization of dental restorative materials is not a linear process, (ii) the exposure reciprocity law is not valid for these materials, and (iii) the polymerization kinetics is affected by the presence of a curing light source and by the presence of an opaque substrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new generation of polymerizable dental resin composite restorative material systems.
the development and characterization of novel, biocompatible and biodegradable polymers and polymer-based materials for biomedical applications.
the study of the polymerization of dental resin composites, with particular emphasis on the study of the exposure reciprocity of the light curing systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymerization of resin composite materials is a non-linear process and the reciprocity law of photochemistry does not apply.
the exposure reciprocity law is valid for the polymerization of composite resins.

the exposure reciprocity of polymerization of resin composite dental restorative materials is not a constant, and the exposure reciprocity varies with the composition and structure of the resin composite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of this study show that the polymerization of a composite resin is not linearly related to the intensity and duration of the curing light, but is related to the total energy delivered to the material.

the polymerization process of composite restorative materials can be divided into two phases: the first one is the initiation phase, where the photoinitiator is activated by the exposure of light and starts the polymerization process, and the second is the propagation phase, which is the actual polymerization of the material.

we have demonstrated that the exposure reciprocity law applies to the polymerization of resin composite materials and that the reciprocity law is valid for the range of exposure times and intensities used clinically.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polymerization of resin composite is a complex process and that there is no simple way to predict how the exposure reciprocity factor will change as a result of a change in the light source.
the exposure time and the intensity of the light source should be considered together when curing resin composite materials.
the exposure reciprocity for resin composite restorations can be achieved by adjusting the light intensity to the light duration.
